detail.longDescription: Today, I found out my Jellyfin instance was dangerous for itself… When I set the whole stack up, I didn’t bother with hardware acceleration, meaning you could hear which machine was streaming a media, given all fans would go full throttle Fast forward to last week, I enabled hardware acceleration, VAAPI to be exact, no more cpu fan ready to take off but… Some medias stutter every few seconds… Why ?! I benchmarked everything, CPU transcoding is 4x the realtime speed of the media, and VAAPI based transcoding is 27x, so that should stutter, right ? No bandwidth issue at any hop either, so I don’t get it.. It turns out, transcoding at 27x the realtime media speed meant also writing much more to disk, in the cache directory This also meant, less IO throughput to read these already transcoded segments, so stuttering… The issue was an IO overload because of a too agressive transcoding speed, I had never seen that before 🫠 # homelab # selfhost # jellyfin # transcode # selfhosting # selfhosted # io # gpu # vaapi
